proposed_branch: Instantiate and submit the trace's distinct mer-B SnCl3F3 ordering, then refine and compare it under the same whole-profile model used for the existing CIFs.
reason: All three submitted P1 CIFs parse as fully occupied, charge-balanced K4Sn2Cl6F6 cells (18 atoms, V = 390.3601 A^3), primitive-standardize without a hidden cell reduction, have distinct ordered structures, complete SnX6 shells, and no short contacts. The tetragonal indexing is strong (all first 20 lines indexed, M(20) = 439.5), and the instantiated primary gives an auditable whole-profile correlation of 0.998501 with RMSE 0.1656, close to the pattern noise. However, the trace also explicitly tested a fourth, mer-B ordering (F direction sets [0,2,3] and [1,4,5] on the two Sn sites) that is absent from the submitted set and is not element-aware structure-matched to any of the three CIFs after primitive standardization. Reinstantiating and refining that branch with the same profile model gives correlation 0.998481 and RMSE 0.1667 (better than submitted alternative-2 by profile MSE), while remaining charge-balanced, overlap-free, and octahedrally coordinated. It therefore has not been quantitatively or chemically rejected and is a concrete materially different viable candidate.
